items.title: Esther Dupuy Breckenridge Interview, 1958-05-14
items.q: where they had the famous Perron himself. And he knew all of our crowd and the ones that were gifted and could dance and sing. And at all the parties, he would act as a sort of massive ceremonies and call on us to get up and do our stuff.

ctx.x: Oh, yes. And private parties and other private parties, Tate-en-sons. The New Orleans Country Club had Tate-en-sons on Saturdays and Sundays, where they had the famous Perron himself. And he knew all of our crowd and the ones that were gifted and could dance and sing. And at all the parties, he would act as a sort of massive ceremonies and call on us to get up and do our stuff. We'd sing, harmonize, dance. You really don't see the young people do that as much as we used to, because that was a golden age of jazz.…
What did your parents think of jazz? Your parents and their friends?
